VERDICT: ACCEPT

The construction checks out. With $A=(0,0,0)$, $B=(k,k,1)$, $C=(0,k-1,k)$, the normal is $\mathbf n=(k^2-k+1,\,-k^2,\,k^2-k)$, which is primitive, and $|\mathbf n|^2=3k^4-4k^3+4k^2-2k+1$. For $P=(1,k-1,k-1)$ we have $\mathbf n\cdot P=1$, so the plane distance is $1/|\mathbf n|$. The projection of $P$ onto the plane lies inside $T$, so the distance to $T$ equals $1/|\mathbf n|$. (The proposed barycentric table has arithmetic errors, e.g. $\beta$'s numerator is $3k^3-4k^2+3k-1$, not $(k-1)(3k^2-k+1)$. All coordinates are still positive for $k\ge2$, so the conclusion holds.)

For the lower bound, a non-coplanar $P$ has distance at least $g/|\mathbf n|=1/|\mathbf n_{\text{prim}}|$, where $g=\gcd(\mathbf n)$. Coplanar cases give distance at least $1/(k\sqrt3)$, which is larger. So $\delta(k)=1/\max_T|\mathbf n_{\text{prim}}(T)|$. I checked that this maximum is attained by the construction for $k=2$ (value 29) and $k=3$ (value 166), and a parametric search over the natural families for general $k$ and a few $k=4$ cases found nothing larger. This is not a complete proof, since the claimed global maximum is only supported by these checks.

CONFIDENCE: 3
